chore(src): delete the dead, and add the check that finds them (S21)

An export is a promise to a caller. This package ships no library — `simt` is the
whole surface — so an exported binding nobody imports is a promise to nobody.

**Deleted outright** (verified dead against `git show HEAD`, one occurrence each):
`gateKind`, `gateWhy`, `gateAdr`, `resetWorkspace`, `tracksIdentity`, `isTty`,
`surfaceFrontmatter`, `workspaceOrNull`, and the `__internals` seams in
`hooks/gates.mjs`, `hooks/dispatcher.mjs` and `hooks/resolve.mjs`.

**Unexported, not deleted**: thirteen bindings that were used only inside their own
file — `sourcePath`, `readChainedShim`, `describeShim`, `redactCommand`,
`DEFAULT_EVENTS`, `unstagedFiles`, `RULE_GLOBS`, `readLimitFindings`, `frameSource`,
`editDistance`, `stackReason`, `candidateLocations`, `isExecutable`. The code is
live; only the export was a claim nobody made good on.

**Two duplicates that had already drifted.** `KNOWN_SUBS` was a hand-kept second
copy of the dispatch table, and it was wrong: it carried `doctor`, which
`commandPath` can never reach, because `doctor` is not a group and that branch runs
only for group paths. `commandPath` now reads `IMPLEMENTED`. `mdcFrontmatter` was a
second construction of frontmatter that `targets.mjs` now derives from the surface
row — and it had a test asserting the copy rather than the behaviour, so it would
have kept passing while the written frontmatter came from somewhere else entirely.

**`test/deadcode.test.mjs`**, three tests: no exported binding without a caller, no
`__internals` seam without an importer, and every `STEPS` entry a path and a number.
The last exists because `STEPS` is empty today and a reader has no way to tell an
empty registry from a deleted one — which would make a declared-but-unimplemented
command succeed with empty output.

Two mistakes worth recording. An ad-hoc scan of mine reported `isExecutable` as dead;
`git show HEAD` found its caller in the same file, and six tests failed before I
checked. And the `__internals` check first asked only whether the word appeared
anywhere — which passed for all four seams, because three other files import their
own. It now matches the import *from that module*, and the mutant that puts a seam
back in `hooks/gates.mjs` fails. Three mutations, three failures, 789/789.
